runs.text: The expenditure approach divides GDP into consumption, investment, government purchases, and net exports. Consumption covers household purchases of final goods and services; investment includes business capital, residential construction, and inventory changes; government purchases pay for current goods and services. Net exports add exports and subtract imports so GDP counts only domestic production, while transfer payments themselves are excluded. A recipient's later purchase is counted separately if it pays for current domestic output.

transcript.sourceText: A business buys a newly produced domestic machine for $2 million; this is investment. Government pays contractors $80 million to repair roads; this is government purchases. An $80 million benefit payment is a transfer and is not counted when sent, though any later household purchase of final goods enters consumption. The expenditure identity classifies the counted spending as C + I + G + NX.

Subtract imports within net exports so foreign production is not counted in domestic GDP.
